title: Box2Bit transfers 150MW grid connection to Blackstone and exits Épila
byline: Cristina Cueto; DCD Have your say
html:
Box2Bit, a subsidiary of Capital Energy, has withdrawn from the Epilon data center project in Spain.

The company is selling the 150MW of grid connection capacity it obtained for the project to Blackstone.

The Government of Aragon declared the project to be of public interest in early 2026, with the first phase scheduled to go live in 2029. But Red Eléctrica denied CPD Edge Solutions, a subsidiary of Box2Bit, access for consumption at the Calatorao 220 kV substation.

Box2Bit announced three data center campuses in Aragón, and none will move forward. The €3.4 billion ($3.75bn) Ebro Campus in Cariñena, which DCD reported on in October 2024 with construction scheduled to begin in late 2025, was ruled out because it fell outside the Ministry’s grid investment plan. The €1 billion ($1.1bn) La Charluca site in Calatayud failed to secure access to the transmission grid, and alternatives involving self-consumption did not materialize.

Epilon, in Épila, has now been added to the list of canned projects, with 150MW of grid connection capacity transferred to Blackstone.

This capacity bolsters Blackstone's Calatorao campus, which already has final planning permission and will provide 430MW in two phases. The associated investment exceeds €13 billion ($14.3bn), according to El Español, compared to the €7.5 billion ($8.2bn) and 300MW in the initial announcement.

The owners of approximately 100 hectares reserved for Epilon have not been paid. According to the mayor of Épila, Jesús Bazán, Box2Bit failed to make the first payment, and its rights to the land expired in May - four months after the declaration of interest.

Bazán has suggested that speculative operations could be taking place: announcing a project, securing land and connection rights, and transferring the latter without actually building.

Grid connection is now treated as a transferable asset, with value independent of the land and the project itself. For developers and investors, the availability of power has become the primary criterion for due diligence, taking precedence over the land parcel or the declaration of public interest.

For government agencies, a declaration of general interest does not guarantee implementation: Epilon obtained one, and it lapsed within months; and the Cariñena project, with planning approval, never even began construction.

This piece was translated from DCD's Spanish site and edited by a member of DCD staff.
summary: Grid power in Spain now treated as transferrable asset
